Consortium: The Tower Going to FIG

Personal Take: I don't know to much about the game, but FIG does not exactly have a pristine reputation, and I expect many people will dislike the idea of indirectly financing Tim "3.3 Million Dollar" Schafer.

I think that it makes more sense that, if their first fund-raiser failed, they should attempt to fix it instead of simply changing the platform and a minor change to the requested amount. It didn't even reach half its goal; I don't see how going to a lesser used platform for funding is going to help.

IIRC projects on FIG do not need to return any money to funder if the project falls flat of its original goal (one of the reason why most gamers are wary of it), so if nothing else, they could make a quick buck with it.

They could do that with the flexible funding on indiegogo as well. I suppose it's an option but a lot of people will probably not bother pledging because a lot of people will think: 'it already failed (a month is not long enough to fix whatever the problem was), so there's something wrong with it'.

True enough. I mean, there's sense behind the logic of this, but in many cases a failure to met financial goals simply can be traced back to lacking PR. Of course, the latter is not exactly to be blamed on the consumer, but I've seen a few interesting projects that ended up being scrapped because the devs couldn't afford anything above word-of-mouth advertising.

in many cases a failure to met financial goals simply can be traced back to lacking PR.

I agree; it's not necessarily the pitch itself that fails but I think trying basically straight away puts forward a bad image (that's me, anyway - I don't follow fund-raising projects a lot so I don't know if it could work). I know developers might not be able to afford creating something new to try again and afford better PR. Some games do amazingly well when good PR is involved, e.g. Bloodstained had a good fund-raiser compared to the Shenmue III fund-raiser, it had a good initial response but it started declining until they announced the PS4 game reward and compared to the Bloodstained fund-raiser the community aspect was wanting.
